pyqs.q: (a) A 1.00 molal aqueous solution of trichloroacetic acid is found to boil at 100.18 °C. Calculate its van't Hoff factor. ($K_b$ for water = 0.512 K kg mol$^{-1}$)

solution.notes: This is the answer the official marking scheme gives. The data are not realistic - trichloroacetic acid is a strong acid and would really give $i > 1$ - but in the exam, calculate with the numbers given.

alt.q: (b) State Henry's law. Find the mole fraction of CO$_2$ in water at 298 K under 760 mm Hg. ($K_H$ for CO$_2$ in water at 298 K = $1.25 	imes 10^6$ mm Hg)

steps.t: Henry's law: at constant temperature, the partial pressure of a gas in the vapour phase is proportional to its mole fraction in the solution, $p = K_H x$.

pyqs.q: (a) Explain, using Henry's law: (i) bends, (ii) anoxia.

points: (i) Bends: at depth divers breathe air at high pressure, so more N$_2$ dissolves in blood. On rising, the pressure falls and the dissolved N$_2$ comes out as bubbles that block capillaries - painful and dangerous.
(ii) Anoxia: at high altitude the partial pressure of O$_2$ is low, so less O$_2$ dissolves in blood and tissues; climbers become weak and cannot think clearly.

alt.q: (b) How does sprinkling salt help clear snow-covered roads in hilly areas? Name the colligative property involved.

points: Salt dissolves in the film of water on the ice and lowers its freezing point, so the ice melts at the prevailing temperature.
Colligative property: depression in freezing point.

pyqs.q: Explain why adding 1 mol of KCl to 1 L of water raises its boiling point, while adding 1 mol of methyl alcohol lowers it.

points: KCl is a non-volatile solute (and gives 2 ions): it lowers the vapour pressure of water, so the solution must be heated more to boil - elevation of boiling point.
Methyl alcohol is a volatile liquid, more volatile than water. It adds its own vapour pressure, so the solution's vapour pressure rises and it boils at a lower temperature.

pyqs.q: State Raoult's law for a solution of volatile components. Give two characteristics of a solution that obeys Raoult's law at all concentrations.

points: For a solution of volatile liquids, the partial vapour pressure of each component is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution ($p_i = x_ip_i^\circ$).
Such a solution is ideal: (i) $\Delta_{mix}H = 0$, (ii) $\Delta_{mix}V = 0$ (also: A-B interactions equal A-A and B-B interactions).

pyqs.q: What type of deviation from Raoult's law does a phenol-aniline mixture show? Give the reason. What happens to the boiling point on mixing?

points: Negative deviation.

A hydrogen bond forms between the phenolic proton and the lone pair on aniline's nitrogen; this A-B attraction is stronger than the A-A and B-B attractions, so the escaping tendency and vapour pressure fall.
The boiling point increases (lower vapour pressure).

pyqs.q: What type of deviation from Raoult's law does an ethanol-acetone mixture show? Give the reason. What happens to the boiling point on mixing?

points: Positive deviation.
Acetone molecules come between ethanol molecules and break some of their hydrogen bonds; the A-B interactions are weaker, so molecules escape more easily and the vapour pressure rises.
The boiling point decreases.

pyqs.q: What type of deviation from Raoult's law does a chloroform-acetone mixture show? Give the reason. What happens to the boiling point on mixing?

points: Negative deviation.
The H of chloroform forms a hydrogen bond with the oxygen of acetone; this stronger A-B attraction lowers the escaping tendency and vapour pressure.
The boiling point increases.

pyqs.q: 10 g of a non-volatile solute in 200 g of water gives a vapour pressure of 31.84 mm Hg at 308 K. Pure water's vapour pressure at 308 K is 32 mm Hg. Find the molar mass of the solute.
(a) Define osmotic pressure. Which has the higher osmotic pressure, 1 M KCl or 1 M glucose? Justify.

points: Osmotic pressure is the excess pressure that must be applied to a solution to prevent osmosis (the entry of solvent through a semipermeable membrane).
1 M KCl, because KCl dissociates into K$^+$ and Cl$^-$ ($i \approx 2$), giving more particles; glucose does not dissociate.

alt.q: (b) Give reasons: (i) an azeotrope distils without any change in composition; (ii) aquatic animals are more comfortable in cold water than in warm water.

points: (i) An azeotrope has the same composition in the liquid and vapour phases, so the distillate is identical to the liquid.
(ii) Gas solubility (including O$_2$) decreases as temperature rises ($K_H$ increases), so cold water holds more dissolved oxygen.

pyqs.q: (a) Find the elevation of boiling point when 3 g of CaCl$_2$ (111 g mol$^{-1}$) is dissolved in 260 g of water, assuming complete dissociation. ($K_b$ = 0.52 K kg mol$^{-1}$)

alt.q: (b) X and Y form an ideal solution. Pure X and pure Y have vapour pressures of 120 and 160 mm Hg. Find the vapour pressure of a solution with equal moles of X and Y. (Also 2023 56/2/1 Q19, 56/2/2 Q20, 56/2/3 Q23.)

pyqs.q: State Raoult's law for a solution of volatile components. Why is the vapour pressure of an aqueous glucose solution lower than that of water?

points: The partial vapour pressure of each volatile component is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution.
Glucose is non-volatile. Its molecules occupy part of the surface, so fewer water molecules escape per second - the vapour pressure falls.

pyqs.q: What is meant by positive deviation from Raoult's law? Give an example. What type of azeotrope does it form?

points: The solution's vapour pressure is higher than Raoult's law predicts, because A-B interactions are weaker than A-A and B-B interactions.
Example: ethanol + acetone (or CS$_2$ + acetone).
Minimum boiling azeotrope (e.g. ethanol-water, about 95% ethanol by volume).

repeats: 2025 compartment 56(B) Q17 (define azeotropes; type formed by negative deviation)

pyqs.q: What is meant by negative deviation from Raoult's law? Give an example. What type of azeotrope does it form?

points: The solution's vapour pressure is lower than Raoult's law predicts, because A-B interactions are stronger than A-A and B-B interactions.
Example: chloroform + acetone (or phenol + aniline).
Maximum boiling azeotrope (e.g. nitric acid 68% + water 32% by mass, b.p. 393.5 K).

pyqs.q: (a) Liquids A and B warm up when mixed. What type of deviation from Raoult's law is this, and why? (b) Why can an azeotropic mixture not be separated by fractional distillation?

points: (a) Negative deviation: heat is released ($\Delta_{mix}H < 0$) because the new A-B attractions are stronger than the A-A and B-B attractions broken.
(b) An azeotrope has the same composition in liquid and vapour, so distillation cannot enrich either component.

pyqs.q: Define osmotic pressure. Why is osmotic pressure measurement preferred for finding the molar masses of macromolecules such as proteins and polymers?

points: Osmotic pressure: the excess pressure that must be applied to a solution to prevent osmosis.
It is measured at room temperature (biomolecules decompose on heating), uses molarity, and is large even for very dilute solutions of these poorly soluble, high-molar-mass substances.

pyqs.q: State Henry's law. Why are aquatic species more comfortable in cold water than in warm water?

points: At constant temperature, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to its partial pressure above the liquid ($p = K_Hx$).
$K_H$ increases with temperature, so gas solubility falls. Cold water holds more dissolved O$_2$.

pyqs.q: (A) Give reasons: (a) food cooks faster in a pressure cooker than in an open pan; (b) when liquids X and Y are mixed, the volume decreases - what deviation is this, and what temperature change would you observe?

points: (a) The high pressure inside the cooker raises the boiling point of water, so cooking happens at a higher temperature.
(b) Negative deviation; the temperature increases (heat is released, $\Delta_{mix}H < 0$).

alt.q: (B) Define azeotrope. What type of azeotrope is formed by negative deviation from Raoult's law? Give an example.

points: Azeotropes are binary mixtures with the same composition in liquid and vapour phases that boil at a constant temperature.
Maximum boiling azeotrope; e.g. 68% HNO$_3$ + 32% water by mass.

pyqs.q: (a) Define molal depression constant. How is it related to the enthalpy of fusion?

points: The depression in freezing point observed in a 1 molal solution (1 mol of non-volatile solute in 1 kg of solvent).
$K_f = \dfrac{R 	imes M_1 	imes T_f^2}{1000 	imes \Delta_{fus}H}$ - it is inversely proportional to the enthalpy of fusion of the solvent.

alt.q: (b) What type of deviation does an ethanol-acetone mixture show? Give a reason. Which type of azeotrope does it form?

points: Positive deviation: ethanol-acetone interactions are weaker than the hydrogen bonds in pure ethanol (and acetone-acetone interactions).
Minimum boiling azeotrope.

pyqs.q: A 6% solution of glucose (180 g mol$^{-1}$) is isotonic with a 2.5% solution of an unknown organic substance. Find the molar mass of the substance.

steps.t: Isotonic solutions have equal molar concentrations (non-electrolytes, same temperature): $\dfrac{6}{180} = \dfrac{2.5}{M}$

solution.notes: Other sets changed the numbers: 4% urea vs 5.2% (56/2/2): 78 g mol$^{-1}$; 3% glucose vs 2.5% (56/2/3): 150 g mol$^{-1}$.

pyqs.q: A solution of 18 g of a non-volatile solute in 200 g of water freezes at 272.07 K. Find the molar mass of the solute. ($K_f$ = 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$)

steps.t: $M_2 = \dfrac{1000 	imes K_f 	imes w_2}{\Delta T_f 	imes w_1} = \dfrac{1000 	imes 1.86 	imes 18}{1.08 	imes 200}$

solution.notes: The marking scheme uses 273.15 K for the freezing point of water.

pyqs.q: Why does a solution of a non-volatile solute boil at a higher temperature than the pure solvent? Why is elevation of boiling point a colligative property?

points: The solute lowers the vapour pressure, so the solution must be heated to a higher temperature before its vapour pressure equals atmospheric pressure.
It depends only on the number of solute particles (molality), not on their nature.

pyqs.q: Calculate the osmotic pressure of a 5% (w/V) urea solution (60 g mol$^{-1}$) at 300 K. ($R$ = 0.0821 L atm K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)

alt.q: OR: Visha took two aqueous solutions - 7.5 g of urea (60 g mol$^{-1}$) in 100 g of water, and 42.75 g of substance Z in 100 g of water - and both froze at the same temperature. Find the molar mass of Z.

steps.t: Same $\Delta T_f$ and same solvent mass, so equal moles: $\dfrac{7.5}{60} = \dfrac{42.75}{M_Z}$

pyqs.q: State Raoult's law for a solution of volatile components. What is the similarity between Raoult's law and Henry's law?

points: The partial vapour pressure of each component is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution.
Both say a volatile component's partial pressure is proportional to its mole fraction in solution; only the constant differs. Raoult's law is the special case of Henry's law with $K_H = p_1^\circ$.

pyqs.q: What happens when (i) a pressure greater than the osmotic pressure is applied on the solution side of a semipermeable membrane separating it from solvent; (ii) acetone is added to pure ethanol?

points: (i) Reverse osmosis: pure solvent flows out of the solution into the solvent side.
(ii) Acetone breaks some hydrogen bonds between ethanol molecules; the solution shows positive deviation from Raoult's law (vapour pressure increases).

repeats: 2020 56/2/3 Q21 (experimental molar mass more than true value; $i$ = 0.4)

pyqs.q: Predict the state of the solute in solution when (a) $i$ = 0.3, (b) $i$ = 4.

points: (a) $i$ < 1: the solute is associated.
(b) $i$ > 1: the solute is dissociated (into ions).

pyqs.q: State Henry's law. Find the solubility (mole fraction) of CO$_2$ in water at 298 K under 760 mm Hg. ($K_H$ = $1.25 	imes 10^6$ mm Hg at 298 K)

steps.t: Henry's law: the partial pressure of a gas in the vapour phase is proportional to its mole fraction in the solution, $p = K_Hx$.

pyqs.q: (a) Which has the higher boiling point, 0.1 molal aqueous glucose or 0.1 molal aqueous KCl, and why? (b) Is the van't Hoff factor less or more than one for CH$_3$COOH in (i) water, (ii) benzene?

points: (a) 0.1 m KCl: it dissociates into two ions, doubling the particle concentration, so $\Delta T_b$ is larger.
(b)(i) In water acetic acid partly ionises: $i$ > 1. (ii) In benzene it dimerises through hydrogen bonding: $i$ < 1.

pyqs.q: Give reasons: (a) aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water than in warm water; (b) people at high altitudes suffer from anoxia and cannot think clearly.

points: (a) Solubility of O$_2$ falls as temperature rises ($K_H$ increases), so cold water contains more dissolved oxygen.
(b) At high altitude the partial pressure of O$_2$ is low; by Henry's law less O$_2$ dissolves in the blood.

alt.q: OR: What type of azeotrope does a solution of acetone and chloroform form? Justify using the intermolecular interactions in the solution.

points: Maximum boiling azeotrope.
Chloroform hydrogen bonds to acetone's oxygen, so A-B attractions are stronger than A-A and B-B: negative deviation, lower vapour pressure, higher boiling point.

pyqs.q: State Henry's law and write two of its applications.

points: At constant temperature, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas above the liquid ($p = K_Hx$).
Soda bottles are sealed under high CO$_2$ pressure to increase CO$_2$ solubility.
Scuba tanks use air diluted with helium to avoid bends (or: low O$_2$ partial pressure at altitude causes anoxia).

pyqs.q: Write two differences between an ideal solution and a non-ideal solution.

points: An ideal solution obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration; a non-ideal solution does not.

Ideal: $\Delta_{mix}H = 0$ and $\Delta_{mix}V = 0$; non-ideal: $\Delta_{mix}H 
eq 0$ and $\Delta_{mix}V 
eq 0$.
(Also: in an ideal solution A-B interactions equal A-A and B-B interactions; in a non-ideal one they are weaker or stronger.)

pyqs.q: (a) What type of deviation from Raoult's law does a mixture of ethanol and acetone show? Give a reason.

points: Positive deviation.
Acetone breaks some hydrogen bonds between ethanol molecules; ethanol-acetone attractions are weaker than those in the pure liquids, so the vapour pressure is higher.

alt.q: (b) Define azeotrope. What type of azeotrope is formed by negative deviation from Raoult's law?

points: A binary mixture with the same composition in liquid and vapour phase that boils at a constant temperature.
Maximum boiling azeotrope (e.g. nitric acid-water).

pyqs.q: (a) Shweta mixed 10 mL each of liquids A and B and got 20.2 mL of solution. (i) Why did the volume change? (ii) Will the temperature rise or fall on mixing? (iii) Give an example of this type of solution.

points: (i) A-B attractions are weaker than A-A and B-B attractions, so molecules move apart: positive deviation ($\Delta_{mix}V > 0$).
(ii) The temperature falls - mixing is endothermic ($\Delta_{mix}H > 0$).
(iii) Ethanol + acetone (or CS$_2$ + acetone).

alt.q: (b) (i) How does sprinkling salt help clear snow-covered roads in hilly areas? (ii) What happens to red blood cells kept in 0.5% (mass/volume) NaCl solution? Justify. (iii) Write an application of reverse osmosis.

points: (i) Salt lowers the freezing point of water (depression in freezing point), so the ice melts.
(ii) They swell and may burst: 0.5% NaCl is hypotonic relative to the cell fluid (isotonic = 0.9%), so water enters the cells by osmosis.
(iii) Desalination of sea water.

Give reasons: (a) osmotic pressure is preferred for finding the molar masses of macromolecules such as proteins and polymers; (b) aquatic animals are more comfortable in cold water than in warm water; (c) the boiling point elevation of 1 M KCl is nearly double that of 1 M sugar solution.

points: (a) Measured at room temperature (biomolecules are unstable when heated), uses molarity, and is large even for very dilute solutions.

(c) KCl dissociates into two ions ($i \approx 2$), doubling the number of particles; sugar does not dissociate.

(I) Adding 100 g of a non-volatile solute A to 1000 g of water reduces the vapour pressure by 50%. Find the molar mass of A. (II) Nitric acid containing 32% water by mass cannot be separated into its components by fractional distillation. Why?

steps.t: (II) It is a maximum boiling azeotrope (68% HNO$_3$, 32% water): liquid and vapour have the same composition.

solution.notes: A 50% lowering is far from dilute, so the exact mole-fraction form must be used (the official scheme does). The tiny molar mass is a quirk of the made-up numbers.

pyqs.q: 70 g of a solute is dissolved in 700 g of solvent; the solution's density is 1.5 g mL$^{-1}$. The ratio molality : molarity is:

pyqs.assertion: Solutions that flow in the bloodstream must always have the same osmotic pressure as blood.
pyqs.reason: Sodium and potassium ions maintain the osmotic pressure balance inside and outside the cells of an organism.
pyqs.explanation: Both true (otherwise cells gain or lose water by osmosis), but the reason does not explain why IV fluids must be isotonic. Official key: B.

pyqs.q: (A) (I) 50 mL of phenol and 50 mL of aniline are mixed. Is the volume equal to, more than or less than 100 mL? Why? (II) Ritesh suggests adding salt to the ice box holding cold drinks to keep them cold longer. Justify.

points: (I) Less than 100 mL: phenol-aniline attraction (hydrogen bonding) is stronger than phenol-phenol and aniline-aniline attraction, so the molecules pack closer (negative deviation).
(II) Salt lowers the freezing point of water, so the ice-salt mixture stays at a lower temperature and the ice lasts longer.

alt.q: (B) (I) BaCl$_2$ and Na$_2$SO$_4$ solutions give a white precipitate when mixed. If they are separated by a semipermeable membrane, will a precipitate appear through osmosis? (II) Why does water stop boiling when sugar is added to it?

points: (I) No - only solvent molecules cross the membrane in osmosis; Ba$^{2+}$ and SO$_4^{2-}$ ions cannot meet.
(II) Sugar lowers the vapour pressure, raising the boiling point above the current temperature.

pyqs.q: Find the vapour pressure of a 1 molal aqueous MgCl$_2$ solution if MgCl$_2$ is 70% dissociated. Pure water's vapour pressure at 25 °C is 23.8 mm Hg.

solution.notes: CBSE's sample marking scheme writes 22.9 mm Hg, but its own expression gives 23.8 × (1 - 2.4/56.5) = 22.79 mm Hg. Either way about 22.8.
